metric_parameters.explanation: Methods longer than this many lines may be too complex and should be refactored.

metric_notes.definition: A Long Method is a routine whose body has grown so large that it mixes several responsibilities and obscures its intent.
metric_notes.calculation: For each function or method, skip property-style accessors, count non-empty and non-comment lines between its start and end, and flag it when that count is greater than LONG_METHOD_LINES.
metric_notes.impact: Overly long methods are hard to read, difficult to test exhaustively, and tend to hide bugs in seldom-visited branches.
metric_notes.mitigation: Refactor by applying Extract Method, Introduce Parameter Object, or Replace Method with Method Object so each helper expresses a single responsibility.

procedure.rule: count non-empty, non-comment lines in the method body
procedure.threshold: if non_comment_loc > LONG_METHOD_LINES then flag

emit.Name: Long Method
emit.Description: Method '<name>' has <non_comment_loc> non-comment lines (> LONG_METHOD_LINES).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with more than this many methods may have too many responsibilities.

metric_notes.definition: A Large Class tries to do too much by accumulating a long list of methods or fields, effectively becoming a grab bag of behavior.
metric_notes.calculation: Ignore dataclasses and exception types, then count non-trivial methods (not magic methods and not one-line getters/setters) and significant attributes; if the non-trivial method count exceeds LARGE_CLASS_METHODS, mark the class as large.
metric_notes.impact: Bloated classes concentrate change risk and entangle unrelated features so that touching one concern can accidentally break another.
metric_notes.mitigation: Use Extract Class or Extract Module to move cohesive subsets of behavior until the remaining class has one clear purpose.

procedure.rule: count non-trivial methods
procedure.threshold: if non_trivial_methods > LARGE_CLASS_METHODS then flag

emit.Name: Large Class
emit.Description: Class '<name>' has <non_trivial_methods> non-trivial methods (> LARGE_CLASS_METHODS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Functions with more than this many primitive parameters may benefit from introducing parameter objects.
Minimum number of arguments required before primitive-obsession detection runs.
Minimum fraction of primitive-typed parameters to flag primitive obsession.

metric_notes.definition: Primitive Obsession is the overuse of basic types such as strings and integers to represent domain ideas rather than small, meaningful objects.
metric_notes.calculation: Scan function signatures and class fields for primitive types (int, str, bool, etc.); when groups of primitives appear together in at least PRIMITIVE_MIN_ARGS arguments or PRIMITIVE_OBSESSION_COUNT fields and the primitive-to-domain ratio exceeds PRIMITIVE_RATIO_THRESHOLD, flag primitive obsession.
metric_notes.impact: Overusing primitives scatters formatting and validation logic, allows illegal states, and hides domain knowledge.
metric_notes.mitigation: Introduce Value Objects, enums, or tiny domain classes to encapsulate the data and its invariants, and pass those abstractions instead of raw primitives.

procedure.rule: find groups of primitive parameters/fields used together and compute primitive-to-domain ratio
procedure.threshold: if group size >= PRIMITIVE_MIN_ARGS and primitive_count >= PRIMITIVE_OBSESSION_COUNT and ratio > PRIMITIVE_RATIO_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Primitive Obsession
emit.Description: Uses <primitive_group_size> primitives together (min args PRIMITIVE_MIN_ARGS, ratio <primitive_ratio> > PRIMITIVE_RATIO_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Functions with more than this many parameters may be trying to do too much.

metric_notes.definition: A Long Parameter List is a function signature that accepts so many arguments that callers struggle to understand or supply them correctly.
metric_notes.calculation: Count explicit parameters for each callable, excluding implicit receivers like self/cls; when the total exceeds LONG_PARAMETER_LIST, mark the signature as a long parameter list.
metric_notes.impact: Large signatures increase coupling and make APIs fragile because every new data point must be threaded through numerous call sites.
metric_notes.mitigation: Group related values into Parameter Objects, pass context objects, or store frequently used data inside the class instead of demanding it in every call.

procedure.rule: count parameters
procedure.threshold: if param_count > LONG_PARAMETER_LIST then flag

emit.Name: Long Parameter List
emit.Description: Function '<name>' has <param_count> parameters (> LONG_PARAMETER_LIST).

metric_parameters.explanation: Groups of parameters appearing together in multiple functions may indicate data clumps.
Minimum parameter-group size to consider for data clumps.

metric_notes.definition: Data Clumps are sets of variables or parameters that always appear together, signaling a missing abstraction.
metric_notes.calculation: Find recurring parameter or field combinations of size at least DATA_CLUMP_MIN_COMBO_SIZE; if the same grouping travels together in DATA_CLUMPS_THRESHOLD or more methods or calls, report a data clump.
metric_notes.impact: Clumped data causes duplicated validation and makes enhancements risky because every copy must be updated consistently.
metric_notes.mitigation: Extract a class or record to represent the concept and replace the parallel parameter lists with a single well-named object.

procedure.rule: find recurring parameter/field combinations of size >= DATA_CLUMP_MIN_COMBO_SIZE across methods/calls
procedure.threshold: if combination recurs >= DATA_CLUMPS_THRESHOLD times then flag

emit.Name: Data Clumps
emit.Description: Group <group_members> recurs <occurrences> times (>= DATA_CLUMPS_THRESHOLD, size >= DATA_CLUMP_MIN_COMBO_SIZE).

metric_parameters.explanation: If-else chains longer than this may indicate a switch statement smell.

metric_notes.definition: The Switch Statements smell appears when complex conditional chains are repeatedly used to select behavior instead of relying on polymorphism or strategy objects.
metric_notes.calculation: Measure the length of conditional chains (if/elif/else or match/case); when the number of branches exceeds COMPLEX_CONDITIONAL or similar decision blocks repeat, treat it as a switch statement smell.
metric_notes.impact: Large conditionals scatter related behavior across several blocks, violating the Open/Closed Principle and making enhancements error-prone.
metric_notes.mitigation: Replace switches with polymorphic subclasses, Strategy implementations, or lookup tables so each variant owns its logic.

procedure.rule: count branches in if/elif/else or match/case chains and detect repeated switches
procedure.threshold: if branches > COMPLEX_CONDITIONAL or chain duplicated then flag

emit.Name: Switch Statements
emit.Description: Conditional chain has <branch_count> branches (> COMPLEX_CONDITIONAL) or repeated switch logic.

metric_parameters.explanation: Fields initialized but not used in most methods may be temporary fields.

metric_notes.definition: A Temporary Field is an instance variable that is set only in special situations and remains unused the rest of the time, cluttering the object.
metric_notes.calculation: Locate attributes initialized in constructors or setters and count how many distinct methods read them; if fewer than TEMPORARY_FIELD_THRESHOLD consumers reference the field, flag it as temporary.
metric_notes.impact: Temporary fields increase cognitive load and can leave objects partially initialized because clients forget to populate rare state.
metric_notes.mitigation: Move the field into a dedicated helper, turn it into a local variable inside the special-case method, or encapsulate the scenario inside its own class.

procedure.rule: find fields set in ctor/setters and count distinct methods that read them
procedure.threshold: if consumer_count < TEMPORARY_FIELD_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Temporary Field
emit.Description: Field '<field>' is used by <consumer_count> methods (< TEMPORARY_FIELD_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with identical sets of methods may be alternative classes with different interfaces.

metric_notes.definition: This smell occurs when two classes represent the same abstraction but expose incompatible method names, forcing clients to know each variation.
metric_notes.calculation: Compare classes that offer similar capabilities; when they implement equivalent operations but expose different method names or signatures and the count of such mismatches exceeds ALTERNATIVE_CLASSES_THRESHOLD, flag them as alternatives with different interfaces.
metric_notes.impact: Clients duplicate adapter code or conditional logic to bridge the mismatched interfaces, increasing coupling and bugs.
metric_notes.mitigation: Align the APIs via Rename Method, Extract Interface, or Adapter so clients can treat the alternatives polymorphically.

procedure.rule: compare classes with similar capabilities for mismatched names/signatures
procedure.threshold: if mismatching equivalents exceed ALTERNATIVE_CLASSES_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces
emit.Description: Classes <class_a>/<class_b> share capability but have > ALTERNATIVE_CLASSES_THRESHOLD interface mismatches.

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with more than this many distinct method name prefixes may be changing for too many reasons.
Classes with more than this many methods changing for different reasons may have divergent change.

metric_notes.definition: Divergent Change describes a class that must be edited in multiple places whenever one business concept evolves because it mixes unrelated responsibilities.
metric_notes.calculation: Group a class's methods by change reason or prefix from DIVERGENT_CHANGE_PREFIXES; if many groups coexist or the largest groups exceed DIVERGENT_CHANGE_METHODS, mark the class as prone to divergent change.
metric_notes.impact: Classes with multiple reasons to change violate the Single Responsibility Principle and raise regression risk.
metric_notes.mitigation: Split the class along responsibility boundaries and move behavior toward the data that truly owns it.

procedure.rule: group methods by change reason/prefix and count groups
procedure.threshold: if multiple sizable groups exist or largest group > DIVERGENT_CHANGE_METHODS then flag

emit.Name: Potential Divergent Change
emit.Description: Class '<name>' has <group_count> change groups; largest group size <largest_group> (> DIVERGENT_CHANGE_METHODS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum similarity between method sets to mark parallel inheritance hierarchies.

metric_notes.definition: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies exist when creating a class in one hierarchy forces the creation of a mirrored class in another hierarchy, duplicating structure.
metric_notes.calculation: Walk inheritance trees and compute similarity of class names/roles across hierarchies; if subclasses must be added in lockstep and similarity surpasses PARALLEL_INHERITANCE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, report parallel inheritance hierarchies.
metric_notes.impact: Every new behavior requires edits in multiple hierarchies, multiplying maintenance effort and inconsistency risk.
metric_notes.mitigation: Collapse the hierarchies through composition, delegate shared behavior to common abstractions, or fuse them into a single tree with polymorphic roles.

procedure.rule: detect paired hierarchies that evolve together
procedure.threshold: if similarity exceeds PARALLEL_INHERITANCE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
emit.Description: Hierarchies <hier_a>/<hier_b> similarity <similarity> (> PARALLEL_INHERITANCE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Methods called in more than this many places may cause shotgun surgery when changed.
Methods called in more than this many different contexts may cause shotgun surgery.
Names to ignore when collecting calls for shotgun surgery detection.

metric_notes.definition: Shotgun Surgery is a form of scattered change where one requirement forces edits in many classes because related logic is dispersed.
metric_notes.calculation: For each change point, count distinct callees or files touched (excluding SHOTGUN_SURGERY_EXCLUDE_NAMES); when calls exceed SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CALLS or touched contexts exceed SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CONTEXTS, flag shotgun surgery risk.
metric_notes.impact: Missing one of the scattered locations can leave the system inconsistent and raises regression rates.
metric_notes.mitigation: Group related behavior into cohesive modules or services so that a feature is implemented in as few places as possible.

procedure.rule: count distinct callees or files touched per feature/change
procedure.threshold: if calls > SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CALLS or contexts > SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CONTEXTS then flag

emit.Name: Potential Shotgun Surgery
emit.Description: Change touches <call_count> calls or <context_count> contexts (> SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CALLS/SHOTGUN_SURGERY_CONTEXTS).

procedure.fallback_guidance: If change_points/touched_files are empty, approximate impact with distinct external calls and how many different modules they touch (call_graph breadth + module fan-out); be conservative and return no finding if breadth is low.

metric_parameters.explanation: Files with more than this ratio of comment lines to total lines may be over-commented.
Comment blocks larger than this may indicate code that needs refactoring.

metric_notes.definition: Excessive Comments indicate code that relies on large explanations because the underlying logic is unclear or overly complex.
metric_notes.calculation: Compute comment density (comment lines divided by total lines) and detect contiguous comment blocks; if density exceeds EXCESSIVE_COMMENTS_RATIO or any block is longer than LARGE_COMMENT_BLOCKS lines, flag excessive commenting.
metric_notes.impact: Comment-heavy code drifts out of date, misleads maintainers, and often hides design problems that should be expressed in code.
metric_notes.mitigation: Refactor the code for clarity with expressive names and smaller functions, keeping only comments that document intent not evident in the code.

procedure.rule: compute comment density and largest block size
procedure.threshold: if density > EXCESSIVE_COMMENTS_RATIO or block_len > LARGE_COMMENT_BLOCKS then flag

emit.Name: Excessive Comments
emit.Description: Comment density <comment_ratio> (> EXCESSIVE_COMMENTS_RATIO) or block length <block_len> (> LARGE_COMMENT_BLOCKS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Functions with identical code may indicate duplication that should be refactored.
Minimum number of lines to consider for duplicate code detection.

metric_notes.definition: Duplicate Code is logic that appears in more than one place with minimal variation.
metric_notes.calculation: Search for identical or highly similar code fragments; if two or more blocks of at least DUPLICATE_CODE_MIN_LINES share similarity above DUPLICATE_CODE_THRESHOLD, record duplicate code.
metric_notes.impact: Fixes and improvements must be applied repeatedly, increasing effort and the risk of inconsistent behavior.
metric_notes.mitigation: Extract the shared behavior into a single method or module and delete the redundant branches so there is one authoritative implementation.

procedure.rule: find identical/near-identical fragments of length >= DUPLICATE_CODE_MIN_LINES
procedure.threshold: if similarity >= DUPLICATE_CODE_THRESHOLD across multiple locations then flag

emit.Name: Duplicate Code
emit.Description: Duplicate block length <lines> similarity <similarity> (>= DUPLICATE_CODE_THRESHOLD) across locations <locations>.

procedure.fallback_guidance: If similarity_scores are empty, rely only on identical fragment hashes; if none exist across files/modules, skip duplicate/redundant flags.

metric_parameters.explanation: Treat classes with at least this many trivial getter/setter methods and no other behavior as data classes.

metric_notes.definition: A Data Class exposes fields or trivial getters and setters but contains little or no domain behavior.
metric_notes.calculation: Count meaningful methods; when a class mostly holds fields and trivial accessors with no more than DATA_CLASS_METHODS non-trivial behaviors, classify it as a data class smell.
metric_notes.impact: Data classes break encapsulation and invite Feature Envy because other classes must orchestrate the data themselves.
metric_notes.mitigation: Move the behavior that uses the data back into the class, enforce invariants internally, or convert it into an immutable value object.

procedure.rule: count non-trivial behaviors
procedure.threshold: if non_trivial_methods <= DATA_CLASS_METHODS then flag

emit.Name: Data Class
emit.Description: Class '<name>' has <non_trivial_methods> non-trivial methods (<= DATA_CLASS_METHODS) and mostly holds data.

metric_parameters.explanation: Functions defined but never called may be dead code.

metric_notes.definition: Dead Code consists of variables, functions, or modules that are never executed or referenced.
metric_notes.calculation: Find definitions (functions, classes, variables) that have no references or executions; if unused counts exceed DEAD_CODE_THRESHOLD, mark them as dead code.
metric_notes.impact: Dead code bloats deployments, confuses readers, and may harbor latent vulnerabilities.
metric_notes.mitigation: Delete unused code or keep it only in version-control history instead of the active branch.

procedure.rule: find unused functions/classes/variables
procedure.threshold: if unused count exceeds DEAD_CODE_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Dead Code
emit.Description: Symbol '<name>' is unused (unused count > DEAD_CODE_THRESHOLD).

procedure.fallback_guidance: If coverage/definitions/references are empty, usage is unknown; only flag when there is clear evidence (e.g., unused parameters and no callers/imports).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with this few methods or fewer may not be pulling their weight.
Flag lazy classes whose non-trivial methods span no more than this many total lines.

metric_notes.definition: A Lazy Class offers so little behavior that it cannot justify its maintenance overhead.
metric_notes.calculation: Measure non-trivial method count and lines of code; if both stay below LAZY_CLASS_METHODS and LAZY_CLASS_LINES, the class does too little and is flagged as lazy.
metric_notes.impact: Superfluous classes add indirection, slow navigation, and complicate refactoring.
metric_notes.mitigation: Inline the class into its primary client or merge its responsibilities with a more cohesive abstraction.

procedure.rule: measure non-trivial method count and LOC
procedure.threshold: if methods < LAZY_CLASS_METHODS and loc < LAZY_CLASS_LINES then flag

emit.Name: Lazy Class
emit.Description: Class '<name>' has <methods> methods and <loc> LOC below LAZY_CLASS thresholds.

metric_parameters.explanation: Abstract classes with no concrete implementations may indicate speculative generality.
An accumulation of unused method parameters suggests an interface is more complex than its current implementation requires, a common sign of over-engineering.

metric_notes.definition: Speculative Generality describes infrastructure written for hypothetical future needs that never arrive.
metric_notes.calculation: Detect abstract hooks, extension points, or unused parameters created for possible futures; when speculative elements exceed SPECULATIVE_GENERALITY_THRESHOLD or unused parameters pass UNUSED_PARAMETERS_THRESHOLD, report speculative generality.
metric_notes.impact: Premature abstractions slow development, confuse maintainers, and require upkeep without providing value.
metric_notes.mitigation: Remove unused hooks, inline abstract layers, and wait for real requirements before introducing extension points.

procedure.rule: detect unused extension points or parameters
procedure.threshold: if speculative elements > SPECULATIVE_GENERALITY_THRESHOLD or unused params > UNUSED_PARAMETERS_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Speculative Generality
emit.Description: Unused hooks/parameters count <speculative_count> exceeds SPECULATIVE_GENERALITY/UNUSED_PARAMETERS thresholds.

metric_parameters.explanation: Methods that call another object's methods/properties more than this many times may belong to that other object.
Multiplier comparing external calls to local calls to help detect feature envy.

metric_notes.definition: Feature Envy occurs when a method relies more on another object's data than on its own state.
metric_notes.calculation: For each method, compare accesses and calls to foreign objects versus its own class; if foreign calls exceed FEATURE_ENVY_CALLS and the foreign-to-local ratio is above FEATURE_ENVY_LOCAL_RATIO, flag feature envy.
metric_notes.impact: Envious methods break encapsulation and create tight coupling, so changes in one class force updates in the other.
metric_notes.mitigation: Move the method toward the data it manipulates or introduce a domain service that owns the shared behavior.

procedure.rule: compare foreign vs local accesses/calls
procedure.threshold: if foreign_calls > FEATURE_ENVY_CALLS and foreign/local ratio > FEATURE_ENVY_LOCAL_RATIO then flag

emit.Name: Feature Envy
emit.Description: Method '<name>' foreign/local access ratio <ratio> (> FEATURE_ENVY_LOCAL_RATIO) with <foreign_calls> foreign calls (> FEATURE_ENVY_CALLS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes that share more than this many fields/methods may be too intimate.
Minimum fraction of shared methods/fields used to flag inappropriate intimacy.

metric_notes.definition: Inappropriate Intimacy describes classes that reach into each other's internals instead of collaborating through clear interfaces.
metric_notes.calculation: Count internal or private members shared between two classes and the fraction of methods touching the partner; when shared members exceed INAPPROPRIATE_INTIMACY_SHARED or the method ratio exceeds INAPPROPRIATE_INTIMACY_METHOD_RATIO, mark inappropriate intimacy.
metric_notes.impact: Tightly coupled classes are hard to change independently and frequently cause cascading regressions.
metric_notes.mitigation: Move responsibilities so each class owns its data, expose well-defined interfaces, or decouple the collaborators with composition.

procedure.rule: count shared private/internal members and fraction of methods accessing partner
procedure.threshold: if shared > INAPPROPRIATE_INTIMACY_SHARED or method_ratio > INAPPROPRIATE_INTIMACY_METHOD_RATIO then flag

emit.Name: Inappropriate Intimacy
emit.Description: Classes <class_a>/<class_b> share <shared_members> internals or method ratio <ratio> exceeds intimacy thresholds.

metric_parameters.explanation: Method call chains longer than this may indicate tight coupling and violate the Law of Demeter.

metric_notes.definition: Message Chains are long sequences of navigation (a.b().c().d) that expose internal structure to clients.
metric_notes.calculation: Trace chained attribute or method accesses; when the chain length surpasses MESSAGE_CHAIN_LENGTH (e.g., a.b().c.d), report a message chain smell.
metric_notes.impact: Chains create brittle coupling. Any change to the middle of the chain requires edits in every caller.
metric_notes.mitigation: Apply Hide Delegate, Introduce Facade, or Extract Method so callers interact with a single object that exposes what they need.

procedure.rule: measure depth of chained attribute/method accesses
procedure.threshold: if chain_length > MESSAGE_CHAIN_LENGTH then flag

emit.Name: Message Chains
emit.Description: Call/attribute chain length <chain_length> (> MESSAGE_CHAIN_LENGTH).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes where more than this ratio of methods simply delegate to another class may be middle men.
Maximum number of delegate targets allowed before a delegating class is no longer considered a middle-man smell.

metric_notes.definition: A Middle Man class primarily delegates to other objects without adding meaningful behavior.
metric_notes.calculation: Measure the portion of methods that simply delegate to collaborators; if the delegation ratio exceeds MIDDLE_MAN_RATIO and the class forwards mostly to MIDDLE_MAN_MAX_DELEGATE_TARGETS targets, flag it as a middle man.
metric_notes.impact: Unnecessary delegation layers add indirection and duplicate change effort for every feature.
metric_notes.mitigation: Inline the middle man or redistribute responsibilities so clients collaborate directly with the real service.

procedure.rule: compute percent of methods that delegate and count delegate targets
procedure.threshold: if delegation_ratio > MIDDLE_MAN_RATIO and targets <= MIDDLE_MAN_MAX_DELEGATE_TARGETS then flag

emit.Name: Middle Man
emit.Description: Class '<name>' delegates <delegation_ratio>% of methods to <= <delegate_targets> targets (> MIDDLE_MAN_RATIO).

metric_parameters.explanation: Modules connected to more than this threshold of total modules may be hub-like dependencies.
Require at least this many total connections before flagging a hub-like dependency.
Minimum number of modules required before hub-like dependency detection runs.
Lower bound for fan_in/fan_out balance ratio when evaluating hub-like modules.
Upper bound for fan_in/fan_out balance ratio when evaluating hub-like modules.

metric_notes.definition: A Hub-like Dependency smell points to a module connected to a disproportionate number of other modules, functioning as a single point of coordination.
metric_notes.calculation: Build the dependency graph and compute combined in-degree and out-degree; flag a module when its degree exceeds HUB_LIKE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD, it has at least MIN_HUB_CONNECTIONS across HUB_MIN_PROJECT_MODULES modules, and its in/out balance stays between HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MIN and HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MAX.
metric_notes.impact: Hubs amplify ripple effects because every change or outage in the hub can disrupt many consumers simultaneously.
metric_notes.mitigation: Split the hub into smaller services, introduce facades to balance call traffic, or move cross-cutting utilities into dedicated modules to reduce coupling.

procedure.rule: evaluate combined degree, spread across modules, and in/out balance
procedure.threshold: if degree > HUB_LIKE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD and connections >= MIN_HUB_CONNECTIONS across HUB_MIN_PROJECT_MODULES and balance between HUB_BALANCE_RATIO_MIN/MAX then flag

emit.Name: Hub-like Dependency
emit.Description: Module '<module>' degree <degree> (> HUB_LIKE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD) across <module_count> modules, balance within HUB_BALANCE ratios.

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum function name length to consider when detecting scattered functionality.
Function names to exclude when detecting scattered functionality.
Minimum number of distinct modules sharing the same function name to treat functionality as scattered.

metric_notes.definition: Scattered Functionality describes a feature whose implementation is spread over many modules without clear ownership.
metric_notes.calculation: Extract feature keywords from function names longer than SCATTERED_MIN_FUNCTION_NAME_LENGTH (ignoring SCATTERED_EXCLUDED_NAMES); if the same feature appears in MIN_SCATTERED_OCCURRENCES or more distinct modules, mark the functionality as scattered.
metric_notes.impact: Any change to the feature requires shotgun surgery across the code base, slowing delivery and increasing defects.
metric_notes.mitigation: Assign feature ownership by consolidating related logic into cohesive modules or services and documenting the boundaries.

procedure.rule: map feature keywords (from names length >= SCATTERED_MIN_FUNCTION_NAME_LENGTH) to modules and count distinct modules
procedure.threshold: if modules_per_feature >= MIN_SCATTERED_OCCURRENCES then flag

emit.Name: Scattered Functionality
emit.Description: Feature '<feature>' spans <module_count> modules (>= MIN_SCATTERED_OCCURRENCES).

metric_parameters.explanation: Minimum number of functions a module must have before checking for redundant abstractions.
Minimum Jaccard similarity between module function sets to mark redundant abstractions.

metric_notes.definition: Redundant Abstractions arise when multiple modules expose nearly identical interfaces or behavior because of copy-and-paste design.
metric_notes.calculation: Compare exported functions across modules; when two modules share at least REDUNDANT_MIN_FUNCTIONS operations with similarity above REDUNDANT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD, treat them as redundant abstractions.
metric_notes.impact: Duplicated abstractions double maintenance effort and drift apart over time, confusing consumers.
metric_notes.mitigation: Merge the abstractions, extract the shared portion into a single service, or differentiate responsibilities so each module has a unique role.

procedure.rule: compare exported functions across modules
procedure.threshold: if shared functions >= REDUNDANT_MIN_FUNCTIONS with similarity >= REDUNDANT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Potential Redundant Abstractions
emit.Description: Modules <module_a>/<module_b> share <shared_functions> functions with similarity <similarity> (>= REDUNDANT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD).

procedure.fallback_guidance: If similarity_scores are empty, rely only on identical fragment hashes; if none exist across files/modules, skip redundancy flags.

metric_parameters.explanation: Modules with more than this many functions may be trying to do too much and should be split.
Ignore god-object detection for modules with fewer than this many public functions.

metric_notes.definition: A God Object centralizes the majority of system knowledge and behavior, violating modular design principles.
metric_notes.calculation: Flag classes that centralize too many responsibilities: if they own more than GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS members and at least MIN_GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS significant behaviors while touching numerous fields, mark them as god objects.
metric_notes.impact: God Objects become change bottlenecks, are hard to test exhaustively, and slow parallel development because most features touch them.
metric_notes.mitigation: Distribute responsibilities into domain services or bounded contexts and keep each class focused on a single cohesive concern.

procedure.rule: identify classes with excessive members and behaviors
procedure.threshold: if fields/methods > GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS and significant behaviors >= MIN_GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS then flag

emit.Name: God Object
emit.Description: Class '<name>' has <fields> fields and <methods> behaviors (> GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS and MIN_GOD_OBJECT_FUNCTIONS).

metric_parameters.explanation: Only evaluate improper API usage when a module makes at least this many API calls.
Modules with more than this threshold of repeated API calls to total calls may have improper API usage.
Minimum repetition count for an API call to be considered in repetition metrics.

metric_notes.definition: Potential Improper API Usage refers to calling library methods in an unsupported order or omitting required calls, which often leads to subtle defects.
metric_notes.calculation: Analyze observed API call sequences; if client code repeats the same API over API_REPETITION_THRESHOLD times, skips required calls despite MIN_API_CALLS expectations, or repeats a pattern more than API_REPETITION_MIN_COUNT, flag potential improper usage.
metric_notes.impact: Incorrect API protocols can corrupt state, leak resources, or open security vulnerabilities.
metric_notes.mitigation: Encapsulate API interactions in well-tested adapters, follow vendor guidelines, and add guard clauses or builders that enforce valid sequences.

procedure.rule: detect deviations from expected call sequences, missing required calls, or excessive repetition
procedure.threshold: if usage violates MIN_API_CALLS expectations, exceeds API_REPETITION_THRESHOLD, or repeats more than API_REPETITION_MIN_COUNT then flag

emit.Name: Potential Improper API Usage
emit.Description: Client call sequence deviates (calls <call_count> vs MIN_API_CALLS or repetition exceeds API_REPETITION thresholds).

procedure.fallback_guidance: If api_call_sequences/doc_patterns are empty, require both strong name/keyword overlap and repeated non-local API calls before flagging; otherwise skip.

metric_parameters.explanation: Module names/patterns to ignore when detecting orphan modules.
Require at least this many modules in the dependency graph before searching for orphan modules.

metric_notes.definition: An Orphan Module has no meaningful incoming or outgoing dependencies, indicating it is unused or not integrated into the system.
metric_notes.calculation: After excluding ORPHAN_EXCLUDED_MODULES and ensuring the project has at least MIN_PROJECT_SIZE modules, flag any module with zero incoming and zero outgoing dependencies as an orphan.
metric_notes.impact: Orphans waste maintenance effort and often signal dead features or incomplete integrations.
metric_notes.mitigation: Remove the module or connect it via clear interfaces and tests if it still provides value.

procedure.rule: find modules with zero in-degree and zero out-degree when project size is sufficient
procedure.threshold: if project modules >= MIN_PROJECT_SIZE and module has no deps then flag

emit.Name: Orphan Module
emit.Description: Module '<module>' has no incoming or outgoing dependencies (project size >= MIN_PROJECT_SIZE).

metric_parameters.explanation: Ignore dependency cycles smaller than this length.
Cyclic dependencies involving more than this many modules are considered problematic.
Minimum cycle length to consider a cycle 'high' when combined with strength.
Minimum cycle strength to consider a cycle 'high' when combined with size.
Module name patterns to ignore when analyzing dependency cycles.

metric_notes.definition: A Cyclic Dependency exists when two or more modules depend on each other directly or indirectly, preventing independent reuse.
metric_notes.calculation: Identify strongly connected components in the dependency graph, skipping CYCLE_EXCLUDED_MODULES; report cycles whose size is between MIN_CYCLE_SIZE and MAX_CYCLE_SIZE, and mark as high when size exceeds CYCLE_HIGH_MIN_SIZE or edge strength exceeds CYCLE_HIGH_MIN_STRENGTH.
metric_notes.impact: Cycles complicate builds, deployment order, and reuse because none of the modules can evolve independently.
metric_notes.mitigation: Break the cycle through Dependency Inversion, interfaces, or service boundaries so the dependency graph becomes acyclic.

procedure.rule: find strongly connected components within size bounds and compute strength
procedure.threshold: if cycle size between MIN_CYCLE_SIZE and MAX_CYCLE_SIZE then flag

emit.Name: Cyclic Dependency
emit.Description: Cycle size <cycle_size> within bounds MIN/MAX; strength <cycle_strength>.

metric_parameters.explanation: Modules with instability higher than this value may be too dependent on other modules and prone to changes.
Only analyze instability for modules with at least this many total dependencies.

metric_notes.definition: An Unstable Dependency indicates that a stable component relies on a more volatile component, violating the Stable Dependencies Principle.
metric_notes.calculation: Compute instability per module as fan_out divided by (fan_in + fan_out); when a more stable module depends on a less stable one by more than UNSTABLE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD and has at least MIN_DEPENDENCIES edges, flag an unstable dependency.
metric_notes.impact: Stable modules inherit churn from volatile components, increasing integration risk.
metric_notes.mitigation: Invert the dependency through interfaces, reorganize modules so stable packages depend only on equally stable ones, or add anti-corruption layers.

procedure.rule: compute instability = fan_out / (fan_in + fan_out) for dependencies
procedure.threshold: if a stable module depends on a less stable one by more than UNSTABLE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD with at least MIN_DEPENDENCIES edges then flag

emit.Name: Unstable Dependency
emit.Description: Stable module depends on less stable module; instability gap <gap> (> UNSTABLE_DEPENDENCY_THRESHOLD, deps >= MIN_DEPENDENCIES).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with more than this many methods may be too complex.

metric_notes.definition: NOM measures how many methods a class defines; unusually high values indicate the class is handling too many responsibilities.
metric_notes.calculation: Count methods defined in each class (optionally excluding trivial accessors); when the total exceeds NOM_THRESHOLD, report high number of methods.
metric_notes.impact: Classes with very high NOM are hard to understand, difficult to test thoroughly, and likely to suffer conflicting edits.
metric_notes.mitigation: Partition the behavior into helper classes or services and keep each class focused on a single cohesive concept.

procedure.rule: count methods per class
procedure.threshold: if method_count > NOM_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Number of Methods (NOM)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' has <method_count> methods (> NOM_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with Weighted Methods per Class (complexity-based) higher than this may be too complex.
Classes with Weighted Methods per Class (parameter-based) higher than this may have too many responsibilities.

metric_notes.definition: WMPC (also known as WMC) weights each method by its internal complexity; high sums mean a class concentrates difficult logic.
metric_notes.calculation: Compute WMPC1 as the sum of cyclomatic complexities and WMPC2 by weighting complexity with parameter count; if either WMPC1 or WMPC2 exceeds their thresholds WMPC1_THRESHOLD or WMPC2_THRESHOLD, flag the class.
metric_notes.impact: High WMPC classes are costly to test and modify because every method contributes significant branching and parameter complexity.
metric_notes.mitigation: Break complex methods apart, distribute responsibilities to collaborators, and simplify algorithms to keep the total weight manageable.

procedure.rule: compute WMPC1 as sum of complexities and WMPC2 as complexity weighted by parameters
procedure.threshold: if WMPC1 > WMPC1_THRESHOLD or WMPC2 > WMPC2_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Weighted Methods per Class (WMPC)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' WMPC1 <wmpc1> or WMPC2 <wmpc2> exceeds WMPC thresholds.

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with more than this many members (methods + fields) may be too large.

metric_notes.definition: SIZE2, defined by Lanza and Marinescu, sums the number of significant methods and fields to capture how large a class has become.
metric_notes.calculation: Calculate SIZE2 by adding public methods and accessed attributes; when that size surpasses SIZE2_THRESHOLD, classify the class as large.
metric_notes.impact: Large SIZE2 values highlight bloated types that hide several responsibilities and slow comprehension.
metric_notes.mitigation: Apply Extract Class or Extract Module so each type owns a cohesive subset of behavior and data.

procedure.rule: SIZE2 = public methods + accessed attributes
procedure.threshold: if SIZE2 > SIZE2_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Large Class (SIZE2)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' SIZE2 value <size2> (> SIZE2_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with more than this many fields may have poor encapsulation.

metric_notes.definition: WAC counts the number of significant attributes in a class; high values indicate bloated state and large possible state spaces.
metric_notes.calculation: Count non-trivial attributes referenced by class methods and apply the configured weight; if the resulting WAC exceeds WAC_THRESHOLD, mark the class as heavy.
metric_notes.impact: State-heavy classes are harder to reason about and often signal missing abstractions or poor encapsulation.
metric_notes.mitigation: Encapsulate clusters of fields into helper objects, remove redundant state, and enforce invariants to keep attribute counts small.

procedure.rule: count non-trivial attributes referenced by methods
procedure.threshold: if WAC > WAC_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Weight of a Class (WAC)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' WAC <wac> (> WAC_THRESHOLD).

elements.metric_name: High Lack of Cohesion of Methods (LCOM)

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with Lack of Cohesion in Methods higher than this may need to be split.

metric_notes.definition: LCOM captures how disjoint a class's methods are; high LCOM means the class groups unrelated responsibilities.
metric_notes.calculation: For every pair of methods, check whether they share at least one field; compute LCOM as non-sharing pairs minus sharing pairs, and flag classes whose LCOM exceeds LCOM_THRESHOLD.
metric_notes.impact: Low cohesion classes are harder to maintain because changing one part often affects unrelated logic.
metric_notes.mitigation: Split the class into cohesive groups of methods or move behavior nearer to the data it manipulates.

procedure.rule: LCOM = non-sharing method pairs minus sharing pairs
procedure.threshold: if LCOM > LCOM_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Lack of Cohesion of Methods (LCOM)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' LCOM <lcom> (> LCOM_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with Response for Class higher than this may be too coupled.

metric_notes.definition: RFC counts the number of methods that can execute in response to a message sent to a class.
metric_notes.calculation: RFC equals the number of class methods plus the distinct external methods they invoke; when RFC is greater than RFC_THRESHOLD, flag the class for high response.
metric_notes.impact: High RFC classes have unpredictable behavior and large test matrices because many operations may execute per call.
metric_notes.mitigation: Narrow the public API, encapsulate collaborations behind helper classes, and reduce outgoing calls to lower RFC.

procedure.rule: RFC = methods + distinct external methods invoked
procedure.threshold: if RFC > RFC_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Response for a Class (RFC)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' RFC <rfc> (> RFC_THRESHOLD).

elements.metric_name: High Number of Classes per Module (NOCC)

metric_parameters.explanation: Modules with more than this many classes may be too complex.
Lower bound for average class weight used to adjust NOCC threshold.
Upper bound for average class weight used to adjust NOCC threshold.
Multiplier applied to NOCC threshold when avg weight is low.
Multiplier applied to NOCC threshold when avg weight is high.

metric_notes.definition: NOCC highlights modules that contain more classes than recommended, implying that the module mixes unrelated concerns.
metric_notes.calculation: Count classes per module and adjust acceptable bounds using NOCC_AVG_WEIGHT_BOUND_LOW/HIGH and NOCC_MULTIPLIER_LOW/HIGH; if the adjusted class count exceeds NOCC_THRESHOLD, report high NOCC.
metric_notes.impact: Overcrowded modules are hard to navigate, complicate dependency management, and often violate packaging rules.
metric_notes.mitigation: Split the module into feature-focused packages and document ownership boundaries to keep each namespace manageable.

procedure.rule: count classes and adjust tolerance using NOCC_AVG_WEIGHT_BOUND_* and NOCC_MULTIPLIER_*
procedure.threshold: if adjusted class count > NOCC_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Number of Classes per Module (NOCC)
emit.Description: Module '<module>' has <class_count> classes (> adjusted NOCC_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with Depth of Inheritance Tree higher than this may be using inheritance excessively.
Base classes treated as framework/kernel classes to be excluded from DIT calculations.

metric_notes.definition: DIT measures how many superclasses exist on the path from a class to the root; deep trees make behavior difficult to predict.
metric_notes.calculation: Count ancestor levels for each class while ignoring configured framework bases; if depth exceeds DIT_THRESHOLD, flag a deep inheritance tree.
metric_notes.impact: Deep hierarchies hide behavior across many ancestors and make changes risky because side effects propagate down the tree.
metric_notes.mitigation: Prefer composition or flatten the hierarchy unless a deep inheritance chain provides clear reuse benefits.

procedure.rule: count inheritance levels
procedure.threshold: if depth > DIT_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: Deep Inheritance Tree (DIT)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' inheritance depth <depth> (> DIT_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Modules with more than this many lines of code may be too large.
Multiplier to allow longer LOC for test modules.
If documentation ratio is below this, allow extra LOC via multiplier.
Multiplier applied to LOC threshold when a module has a low code/documentation complexity ratio.

metric_notes.definition: High LOC files contain more lines than recommended for comfortable comprehension and maintenance.
metric_notes.calculation: Count logical lines excluding blanks and comments; adjust the allowed limit for test files via LOC_TEST_FILE_MULTIPLIER and for doc-heavy modules using LOC_DOC_COMPLEXITY_RATIO_BREAKPOINT with LOC_DOC_COMPLEXITY_MULTIPLIER; when effective LOC exceeds LOC_THRESHOLD, flag it.
metric_notes.impact: Large files hide multiple concerns, slow navigation, and cause merge conflicts because many developers touch the same file.
metric_notes.mitigation: Extract classes, modules, or helper functions so each file covers a single cohesive concept.

procedure.rule: count logical LOC excluding blanks/comments; adjust allowed limit for tests and doc-heavy modules via multipliers
procedure.threshold: if effective LOC > effective LOC_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Lines of Code (LOC)
emit.Description: File '<file>' has <loc> LOC (> effective LOC_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Classes with Message Passing Coupling higher than this may be too coupled.
Weight applied to external calls when computing weighted MPC.

metric_notes.definition: MPC counts the number of distinct method invocations a class makes; high MPC indicates strong coupling to many collaborators.
metric_notes.calculation: Count distinct method calls issued by the class, weighting external calls by MPC_EXTERNAL_WEIGHT; if the weighted total exceeds MPC_THRESHOLD, mark high MPC.
metric_notes.impact: Classes with high MPC rely on numerous collaborators, making changes and tests expensive because many dependencies must be coordinated.
metric_notes.mitigation: Introduce facades or mediators, limit outgoing dependencies, and encapsulate collaborations behind smaller service interfaces.

procedure.rule: weight external calls by MPC_EXTERNAL_WEIGHT and sum distinct calls
procedure.threshold: if MPC > MPC_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Message Passing Coupling (MPC)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' MPC <mpc> (> MPC_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Modules with Coupling Between Object Classes higher than this may be too coupled.
Weight applied to direct coupling when computing weighted CBO.
Weight applied to indirect coupling when computing weighted CBO.

metric_notes.definition: CBO measures how many other classes a class depends on; high coupling makes the class brittle and hard to reuse.
metric_notes.calculation: Combine counts of direct dependencies weighted by CBO_DIRECT_WEIGHT and indirect ones weighted by CBO_INDIRECT_WEIGHT; when the total surpasses CBO_THRESHOLD, flag high CBO.
metric_notes.impact: Highly coupled classes break whenever collaborators change and are difficult to unit test in isolation.
metric_notes.mitigation: Introduce interfaces, use dependency injection, and keep dependencies explicit and minimal.

procedure.rule: weighted sum: direct deps * CBO_DIRECT_WEIGHT + indirect deps * CBO_INDIRECT_WEIGHT
procedure.threshold: if CBO > CBO_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Coupling Between Object Classes (CBO)
emit.Description: Entity '<name>' CBO <cbo> (> CBO_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Projects with more than this many classes may be too large or complex.
LOC breakpoint to treat a project as large for NOC threshold adjustment.
LOC breakpoint for medium-sized projects used in NOC threshold adjustment.
Multiplier applied to NOC threshold for very large projects.
Multiplier applied to NOC threshold for medium projects.

metric_notes.definition: NOC counts direct subclasses; unusually high counts suggest an overly general base class that is hard to modify safely.
metric_notes.calculation: Count direct subclasses and adjust tolerance using NOC_LOC_BREAKPOINT_* and NOC_LOC_MULTIPLIER_*; if the adjusted child count exceeds NOC_THRESHOLD, flag high NOC.
metric_notes.impact: Changes to a widely inherited base class ripple to many subclasses, increasing regression risk.
metric_notes.mitigation: Split the hierarchy, push behavior down, or replace inheritance with composition where feasible.

procedure.rule: adjust tolerance using NOC_LOC_BREAKPOINT_* and NOC_LOC_MULTIPLIER_* then compare child count
procedure.threshold: if children > adjusted NOC_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Number of Children (NOC)
emit.Description: Class '<name>' has <children> children (> adjusted NOC_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Methods with cyclomatic complexity higher than this may be too complex and hard to maintain.

metric_notes.definition: Cyclomatic Complexity measures the number of independent execution paths through a method; high values indicate convoluted logic.
metric_notes.calculation: For each method, compute 1 plus the number of decision points (if/elif/for/while/try/except/and/or/ternary); when the score exceeds CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD, flag high complexity.
metric_notes.impact: Complex functions are harder to test exhaustively and more prone to defects when modified.
metric_notes.mitigation: Break the function into smaller helpers, flatten nested logic, or replace conditionals with polymorphism.

procedure.rule: complexity = 1 + number of decision points
procedure.threshold: if complexity > CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD then flag

emit.Name: High Cyclomatic Complexity
emit.Description: Method '<name>' complexity <complexity> (> CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY_THRESHOLD).

metric_parameters.explanation: Modules with more outgoing dependencies than this may be too coupled to other modules.

metric_notes.definition: Fan-out counts how many other modules a component depends upon; high fan-out signals excessive outward coupling.
metric_notes.calculation: Count unique outgoing dependencies per module or class (excluding standard libraries); if the count exceeds MAX_FANOUT, report high fan-out.
metric_notes.impact: Modules with large fan-out inherit churn from many collaborators and are hard to reuse independently.
metric_notes.mitigation: Introduce facades, limit direct dependencies, and keep modules focused on a single responsibility.

procedure.rule: count unique outgoing dependencies
procedure.threshold: if fan_out > MAX_FANOUT then flag

emit.Name: High Fan-out
emit.Description: Entity '<name>' fan-out <fan_out> (> MAX_FANOUT).

metric_parameters.explanation: Modules with more incoming dependencies than this may be too central or have too many responsibilities.

metric_notes.definition: Fan-in counts how many modules depend on a component; high fan-in highlights choke points in the architecture.
metric_notes.calculation: Count unique incoming dependencies while excluding intentional utility modules; when the count exceeds MAX_FANIN, flag high fan-in.
metric_notes.impact: Choke-point modules become single points of failure and make refactoring risky because many consumers rely on them.
metric_notes.mitigation: Split the module into bounded services or publish stable interfaces so consumers depend on smaller slices.

procedure.rule: count unique incoming dependencies
procedure.threshold: if fan_in > MAX_FANIN then flag

emit.Name: High Fan-in
emit.Description: Entity '<name>' fan-in <fan_in> (> MAX_FANIN).

procedure.fallback_guidance: If incoming_dependencies are empty, compute fan_in from dependency edges if present; if both in/out edges are absent, treat dependency data as unknown (not zero) and avoid high fan-in flags.

metric_parameters.explanation: Files with more lines than this may be too large and should be split.

metric_notes.definition: A Long File smell indicates a source file whose length exceeds recommended limits, suggesting that multiple concerns are combined.
metric_notes.calculation: Count meaningful lines per file (non-blank, non-comment); when the total is greater than MAX_FILE_LENGTH, flag a long file.
metric_notes.impact: Huge files hinder navigation, increase merge conflicts, and discourage reuse of embedded logic.
metric_notes.mitigation: Split the file into focused modules or classes and keep each file scoped to a single concept.

procedure.rule: count meaningful lines (non-blank, non-comment)
procedure.threshold: if file_loc > MAX_FILE_LENGTH then flag

emit.Name: Long File
emit.Description: File '<file>' has <loc> meaningful LOC (> MAX_FILE_LENGTH).

metric_parameters.explanation: Methods with more branches (if/else, switch cases) than this may be too complex.
Code with nesting depth greater than this may be too complex and hard to read.
Method prefixes to exclude from branch-count-based smell detection.
Decorators whose methods should be excluded from branch checks.

metric_notes.definition: Too Many Branches describes methods whose number of control-flow constructs exceeds what developers can safely reason about.
metric_notes.calculation: For each method not excluded by BRANCH_EXCLUDE_METHOD_PREFIXES or BRANCH_EXCLUDE_DECORATORS, count branch points and nesting depth; flag the method if branches exceed MAX_BRANCHES or nesting exceeds MAX_NESTING_DEPTH.
metric_notes.impact: Branch-heavy methods are error-prone, hard to test thoroughly, and frequently hide duplicated logic.
metric_notes.mitigation: Flatten nested conditionals, replace control flags with polymorphism, and split logic into smaller helper methods.

procedure.rule: count decision points and max control-flow nesting per method
procedure.threshold: if branch_count > MAX_BRANCHES or max_nesting > MAX_NESTING_DEPTH then flag

emit.Name: Too Many Branches
emit.Description: Method '<name>' has <branch_count> branches and nesting <max_nesting> exceeding thresholds.
